items.title: Bitcoin miners were hijacked and their BTC rewards redirected to an attacker
items.summary: Luxor said just over a dozen customers were affected and will be reimbursed after their machines were redirected to another mining pool.

items.title: Bitcoin's biggest bet is now a drop below $60,000, not a rally above $100,000
items.summary: The $60,000 put has replaced the $100,000 call as bitcoin's biggest options bet on Deribit, with $900 million in open interest after the recent slide.

items.title: Luxor hit by AI-enabled attack that redirected client hashrate, says vulnerability patched
items.summary: The company said it patched the vulnerability within two hours and that no data was leaked or exfiltrated.

items.title: Luxor CEO warns of AI 'dark forest' following Bitcoin miner hijack
items.summary: Attackers redirected customers' Bitcoin mining power through Luxor's Commander platform over the weekend, prompting its CEO to issue a warning to crypto businesses.

items.title: US sellers drive Bitcoin crash, Jensen plots Nvidia comeback: Hodler's Digest
items.summary: Anchorage Digital data suggests the Bitcoin selloff is being driven by US investors. A "war room" has been set up by supporters to reinstate Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.

items.title: CZ denies Binance sold crypto as Bitcoin bounces from four-month low near $62,000
items.summary: The price moves across the market led to $2 billion in crypto liquidations in a single 24-hour period over the weekend.

items.title: Luxor Confirms Bitcoin Mining Hack and Reveals AI-Enabled Attack
items.summary: Luxor Technology has confirmed an unauthorized redirection of bitcoin mining hashrate through its Commander platform, ending speculation surrounding an alleged attack involving thousands of mining machines. The company says the incident was contained within two hours, and affected customers will receive full compensation…

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $2.1 Billion in November as Outflow Streak Hits Seven Days
items.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $185.4 million on Friday, their seventh straight day of outflows, pushing November losses to about $2.1 billion as Bitcoin fell toward $64,000.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose $1 billion for the second week in a row as crypto funds, except one…
items.summary: U.S. spot crypto ETFs lost about $1.55 billion combined, and Avalanche funds' $227,000 was the only weekly inflow among the 15 categories SoSoValue tracks.

items.title: Bitcoin crashes to 3-month low below $63,000 as analyst flags fourth capitulation wave
items.summary: "They are now selling at the very price they wish they had taken advantage of three months ago," wrote James Check.
